claim: Myelin, made by oligodendrocytes, is essential for rapid information transfer in the central nervous system.
source: Myelin, made by oligodendrocytes, is essential for rapid information transfer in the central nervous system.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in neuroscience supported by extensive prior research.

claim: Murine oligodendrocyte precursors in white matter express AMPA receptor subunits GluA2, GluA3 and GluA4.
source: Murine OPs in white matter express AMPA receptor (AMPAR) subunits GluA2, GluA3 and GluA4.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: In Gria2/3 double-knockout mice, approximately 25% fewer oligodendrocytes survived in the subcortical white matter during development.
source: In both double- and triple-knockouts OP proliferation and number were unchanged but ~25% fewer oligodendrocytes survived in the subcortical white matter during development.
evidence: Supported by cell counting data presented in Figure 7B showing reduced CC1+ oligodendrocyte density.

claim: In triple knockout mice (Gria2/3/4), the oligodendrocyte deficit persisted into adulthood.
source: In triple knockouts, this shortfall persisted into adulthood.
evidence: Supported by cell counting data at P53 shown in Figure 10B.

claim: The oligodendrocyte deficit resulted in approximately 20% fewer myelin sheaths.
source: The oligodendrocyte deficit resulted in ~20% fewer myelin sheaths but the average length, number and thickness of myelin internodes made by individual oligodendrocytes appeared normal.
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy data showing reduced density of myelinated axons in Figure 8B.

claim: The average length, number and thickness of myelin internodes made by individual oligodendrocytes appeared normal in AMPAR knockout mice.
source: The oligodendrocyte deficit resulted in ~20% fewer myelin sheaths but the average length, number and thickness of myelin internodes made by individual oligodendrocytes appeared normal.
evidence: Supported by dye-filling experiments (Figures 8C,D) and g-ratio measurements (Figures 8G,H).

claim: AMPAR-mediated signalling from active axons stimulates myelin production in developing white matter by enhancing oligodendrocyte survival.
source: Thus, AMPAR-mediated signalling from active axons stimulates myelin production in developing white matter by enhancing oligodendrocyte survival, without influencing myelin synthesis per se.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing increased apoptosis and reduced oligodendrocyte numbers without changes in myelin per cell.

claim: Myelination of axons by oligodendrocytes enables fast and energy-efficient propagation of electrical signals in the central nervous system.
source: Myelination of axons by oligodendrocytes (OLs), which develop postnatally from proliferating oligodendrocyte precursors (OPs), enables fast and energy-efficient propagation of electrical signals in the central nervous system (CNS).
evidence: This is established knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: Myelin decreases the capacitance of axons and dramatically increases the speed of action potentials.
source: By decreasing the capacitance of axons, myelin dramatically increases the speed of action potentials and reduces the energy demands of the axons.
evidence: This is well-established knowledge about myelin function.

claim: Ensheathing oligodendrocytes can transfer energy substrates into axons.
source: Moreover, the ensheathing OLs can transfer energy substrates into axons (Fünfschilling et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2012b; Saab et al., 2016) possibly supporting them during periods of high metabolic demand.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Synthesis of myelin requires a large investment of energy.
source: Synthesis of myelin requires a large investment of energy (Harris and Attwell, 2012), so it seems likely that myelination evolved to focus on active axons, rather than axons that are electrically silent because, for example, they are still elongating, or they are excess to requirements and destined for developmental pruning.
evidence: Supported by citation to Harris and Attwell, 2012.

claim: Myelination likely evolved to focus on active axons rather than electrically silent axons.
source: Synthesis of myelin requires a large investment of energy (Harris and Attwell, 2012), so it seems likely that myelination evolved to focus on active axons, rather than axons that are electrically silent because, for example, they are still elongating, or they are excess to requirements and destined for developmental pruning.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the energy cost of myelination.

claim: Oligodendrocytes that differentiate in culture from purified OPs can myelinate fixed axons and synthetic nanofibres in vitro.
source: OLs that differentiate in culture from purified OPs can myelinate fixed axons and synthetic nanofibres in vitro, so electrically active axons are not essential for myelination (Rosenberg et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2012a; Bechler et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Electrically active axons are not essential for myelination.
source: OLs that differentiate in culture from purified OPs can myelinate fixed axons and synthetic nanofibres in vitro, so electrically active axons are not essential for myelination (Rosenberg et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2012a; Bechler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from cited in vitro studies.

claim: Electrical activity can modulate myelination by influencing the proliferation and/or differentiation of OPs.
source: Nevertheless, many in vitro and in vivo studies suggest that electrical activity can modulate myelination by influencing the proliferation and/or differentiation of OPs, thus determining the number of OLs that are available to myelinate (Barres and Raff, 1993; Demerens et al., 1996; Li et al., 2010; Gibson et al., 2014; Fannon et al., 2015; Etxeberria et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior published work.

claim: Electrical activity can influence the process of myelination by oligodendrocytes.
source: In addition, electrical activity can influence the process of myelination by OLs (Hines et al., 2015; Mensch et al., 2015; Wake et al., 2011; Lundgaard et al., 2013; Wake et al., 2015; Etxeberria et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior published work.

claim: Oligodendrocyte production and myelination in juvenile or adult mice are influenced by experience.
source: OL production and myelination in juvenile or adult mice are also influenced by experience, presumably via altered neuronal activity (Simon et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2012; Makinodan et al., 2012; Mangin et al., 2012; Sampaio-Baptista et al., 2013; Hill et al., 2014; McKenzie et al., 2014; Xiao et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior published work.

claim: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells express ligand-gated channels including AMPA/kainate and NMDA receptors for glutamate.
source: OL lineage cells can sense the release of neurotransmitter directly, because they express ligand-gated channels (reviewed by Larson et al., 2016), including AMPA/kainate and NMDA receptors for the excitatory transmitter glutamate.
evidence: Supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Oligodendrocyte precursors receive direct AMPA receptor-mediated synaptic input from unmyelinated or partially myelinated axons in all brain regions examined.
source: OPs receive direct AMPA receptor (AMPAR)-mediated synaptic input from unmyelinated or partially myelinated axons in all brains regions examined so far (Bergles et al., 2000; Chittajallu et al., 2004; Lin and Bergles, 2004; Lin et al., 2005; Ge et al., 2006; Kukley et al., 2007; Ziskin et al., 2007; Káradóttir et al., 2008; Müller et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior published work.

claim: Synaptic input to oligodendrocyte precursors is maintained during OP division.
source: Synaptic input is maintained during OP division (Kukley et al., 2008; Ge et al., 2009) but is down-regulated as OPs differentiate into OLs (Cahoy et al., 2008; De Biase et al., 2010; Kukley et al., 2010), suggesting that it might be important in the control of OL development.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Synaptic input is down-regulated as OPs differentiate into oligodendrocytes.
source: Synaptic input is maintained during OP division (Kukley et al., 2008; Ge et al., 2009) but is down-regulated as OPs differentiate into OLs (Cahoy et al., 2008; De Biase et al., 2010; Kukley et al., 2010), suggesting that it might be important in the control of OL development.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Blocking vesicular release from neurons in vitro reduced myelination without much affecting oligodendrocyte numbers.
source: In support of the idea that neurotransmitters regulate myelination, blocking vesicular release from neurons in vitro (Wake et al., 2011, 2015) or in genetically manipulated zebrafish (Hines et al., 2015; Mensch et al., 2015; Koudelka et al., 2016) reduced myelination without much affecting OL numbers.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Blocking glutamate uptake into secretory vesicles in retinal ganglion cells in early postnatal mice increased the number of oligodendrocytes that developed in the optic tract.
source: Conversely, blocking glutamate uptake into secretory vesicles in retinal ganglion cells in early postnatal mice increased the number of OLs that developed in the optic tract, suggesting that glutamate signalling negatively regulates OL development (Etxeberria et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Etxeberria et al., 2016.

claim: NMDA receptor-mediated signalling in oligodendrocyte lineage cells has been suggested to accelerate the myelination of active axons.
source: Glutamate-evoked NMDA receptor (NMDAR)-mediated signalling in OL lineage cells has been suggested to accelerate the myelination of active axons (Lundgaard et al., 2013), which might occur by NMDAR activation up-regulating glucose transport into developing OLs (Saab et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Pharmacological block of AMPAR-mediated signalling in OPs in vitro promotes proliferation and differentiation of OPs.
source: pharmacological block of AMPAR-mediated signalling in OPs in vitro promotes proliferation and differentiation of OPs (Gallo et al., 1996; Yuan et al., 1998; Fannon et al., 2015) but decreases myelination (Fannon et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Pharmacological block of AMPAR-mediated signalling in OPs in vitro decreases myelination.
source: pharmacological block of AMPAR-mediated signalling in OPs in vitro promotes proliferation and differentiation of OPs (Gallo et al., 1996; Yuan et al., 1998; Fannon et al., 2015) but decreases myelination (Fannon et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Fannon et al., 2015.

claim: Gria2, Gria3 and Gria4 are expressed by many small cells in the postnatal day 1 and P14 subcortical white matter.
source: We found that Gria2, Gria3 and Gria4 are expressed by many small cells in the postnatal day 1 (P1) and P14 SCWM (Figure 1).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Gria1 was expressed by very few cells in the subcortical white matter, which were neurons.
source: In contrast, Gria1 was expressed by very few cells in the SCWM, which NeuN labelling showed were neurons (Figure 1A–C and not shown).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization and NeuN labeling data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Olig2 was expressed in 88 ± 3% of Gria2+ cells in white matter.
source: Olig2 was expressed in 88 ± 3% of Gria2+ cells (817 cells counted in four mice), 94 ± 4% of Gria3+ cells (506 cells from three mice) and 90 ± 0.3% of Gria4+ cells (560 cells from three mice) (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by fluorescence ISH and immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Olig2 was expressed in 94 ± 4% of Gria3+ cells in white matter.
source: Olig2 was expressed in 88 ± 3% of Gria2+ cells (817 cells counted in four mice), 94 ± 4% of Gria3+ cells (506 cells from three mice) and 90 ± 0.3% of Gria4+ cells (560 cells from three mice) (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by fluorescence ISH and immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Olig2 was expressed in 90 ± 0.3% of Gria4+ cells in white matter.
source: Olig2 was expressed in 88 ± 3% of Gria2+ cells (817 cells counted in four mice), 94 ± 4% of Gria3+ cells (506 cells from three mice) and 90 ± 0.3% of Gria4+ cells (560 cells from three mice) (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by fluorescence ISH and immunolabeling data shown in Figure 2.

claim: GluA2 is expressed by the majority of oligodendrocyte precursors.
source: Double ISH for Pdgfra and Gria2 followed by immunolabelling for Olig2 indicated that GluA2 is expressed by the majority of OPs (Figure 2D), consistent with previous electrophysiological findings (Kukley et al., 2007; Ziskin et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by double ISH data shown in Figure 2D and citations to prior electrophysiological studies.

claim: GluA2-4 are the main AMPAR subunits expressed by oligodendrocyte lineage cells in the developing mouse subcortical white matter.
source: Together, these data indicate that GluA2-4 are the main AMPAR subunits expressed by OL lineage cells in the developing mouse SCWM.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ISH data presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Gria3 germline knockout mice have no overt neural phenotype.
source: Gria3 germline knockout (KO) mice have no overt neural phenotype (Meng et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Meng et al., 2003.

claim: Gria2 germline knockouts display a range of behavioural abnormalities, including reduced exploratory and reproductive activity and impaired motor coordination.
source: Gria2 germline KOs have higher than normal mortality; the survivors are anatomically normal but display a range of behavioural abnormalities, including reduced exploratory and reproductive activity and impaired motor coordination (Jia et al., 1996; Gerlai et al., 1998; Jia et al., 2001; Shimshek et al., 2006a).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Gria2/3 double knockouts develop tremor starting in the second postnatal week.
source: Gria2/3 double KOs were reported also to develop tremor, starting in the second postnatal week (Meng et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Meng et al., 2003.

claim: The density of Pdgfra+ OPs in the subcortical white matter was unaltered in Gria3null mice compared to wild type littermates at P14 and P21.
source: The density (cells per mm2) of Pdgfra+ OPs in the SCWM was unaltered in Gria3null mice compared to wild type littermates at both ages (p=0.66 at P14; p=0.7 at P21, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 3A,D)
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: There was no change in the density of CC1+ oligodendrocytes in Gria3null mice compared to wild type at P14 and P21.
source: and there was no change in the density of CC1+ OLs (p=0.66 at P14; p=0.7 at P21, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 3B,E).
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: There was no significant difference in the fraction of Pdgfra+ OPs that incorporated EdU in Gria3null mice versus wild type controls at P14.
source: There was no significant difference in the fraction of Pdgfra+ OPs that incorporated EdU in Gria3null mice versus wild type controls (p=0.66, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 3C,F), indicating that the proliferation rate of OPs was not affected by loss of GluA3.
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Loss of GluA3 alone does not detectably affect postnatal oligodendrocyte production or myelination.
source: Therefore, loss of GluA3 alone does not detectably affect postnatal OL production or myelination.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: In Sox10-Cre: Rosa-YFP mice, 96.4% ± 1.0% of Sox10+ cells expressed YFP in the subcortical white matter at P14.
source: In the SCWM at P14, 96.4% ± 1.0% of Sox10+ cells expressed YFP (5551 cells counted in four mice; Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In Sox10-Cre: Rosa-YFP mice, 97.1 ± 0.7% of Sox10+ cells expressed YFP in the cortex at P14.
source: In the cortex, 97.1 ± 0.7% of Sox10+ cells expressed YFP (2506 Sox10+ cells counted in four mice; Supplementary Figure 4—figure supplement 2B), confirming that Cre was active in the great majority of OL lineage cells in both grey and white matter.
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The rectification index was significantly reduced in Gria2–/– mice compared to Gria2+/– and Gria2+/+.
source: The rectification index (RI), defined as (kainate-mediated current amplitude at +17 mV)/ (current amplitude at –63 mV), was significantly reduced in Gria2–/– mice compared to Gria2+/– and Gria2+/+ (p<10–4, one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc test; Figure 4D), confirming that GluA2 had been successfully deleted.
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The kainate-evoked current density at –63 mV in Gria2–/– OPs was not significantly reduced compared to Gria2+/– or Gria2+/+.
source: Despite this, the kainate-evoked current density (current normalized to membrane capacitance, which is proportional to cell surface area) at –63 mV in Gria2–/– OPs was not significantly reduced compared to Gria2+/– or Gria2+/+ (p=0.73, Kruskal-Wallis test; Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: There were no significant changes in the densities of either Pdgfra+ OPs or CC1+ oligodendrocytes in Gria2–/– mice at P14.
source: There were no significant changes in the densities of either Pdgfra+ OPs (p=0.34, Mann-Whitney test; >600 cells counted per mouse) or CC1+oligodendrocytes (p=0.40, Mann-Whitney test; >900 cells counted per mouse) at P14.
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: There were no significant differences in the fractions of EdU+ Pdgfra+ OPs in Gria2–/– versus Gria2+/–.
source: There was no significant difference between the EdU labelling indices of Pdgfra+ OPs in Gria2–/– versus Gria2+/– (p=0.94, Mann-Whitney test), indicating that the cell cycle time of OPs was not affected (Figure 4G,I).
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Oligodendrocyte development is normal in the absence of GluA2.
source: These results demonstrate that OL development is normal in the absence of GluA2, despite the altered AMPAR Ca2+ permeability.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 4.

claim: The rectification index was significantly reduced in Gria3null2–/– mice compared to Gria3null2+/– and Gria3null2+/+ controls.
source: The rectification index was significantly reduced in Gria3null2–/– mice compared to Gria3null2+/– and Gria3null2+/+ controls (p<10−4, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post-hoc test; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Gria3null2–/– mice were viable and survived into adulthood without neurological signs.
source: Gria3null2–/– mice were viable and survived into adulthood without neurological signs, suggesting that the tremor reported in Gria2/3 germline KO mice (Meng et al., 2003) was not related to impaired AMPAR signalling in OL lineage cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the study with an inference about the source of tremor in germline knockouts.

claim: The kainate-evoked current density was approximately 47% less in Gria3null2–/– compared to Gria3null2+/+ controls.
source: Normalizing the amplitude of the maximum kainate-evoked current at –63 mV to the cell size (assessed as membrane capacitance) revealed a significant (~47%) reduction in the current density for Gria3null2–/– compared to Gria3null2+/+ controls (p<10–4, Student's t-test; Figure 5B), indicating that the number of AMPARs expressed on the cell surface was decreased in Gria3null2–/– mice.
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In both Gria3null2–/– and Gria3null2+/+ OPs, kainate-evoked currents were blocked by approximately 80% in the presence of GYKI-52466.
source: In both Gria3null2–/– and Gria3null2+/+ OPs, kainate-evoked currents were blocked by ~80% in the presence of GYKI (Figure 5A,C), confirming that most of the kainate-evoked current is AMPAR-mediated under our experimental conditions.
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: There was no evidence for up-regulation of Gria1 mRNA in Gria3null2–/– subcortical white matter relative to Gria3null2+/+.
source: However, by ISH we found no evidence for up-regulation of Gria1 mRNA in Gria3null2–/– SCWM relative to Gria3null2+/+ (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by ISH data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The majority of AMPARs formed in Gria3null2–/– OPs are probably homo-tetramers of GluA4.
source: Thus, the majority of AMPAR formed in Gria3null2–/– OPs are probably homo-tetramers of GluA4.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of Gria1 upregulation and the presence of GluA4.

claim: Neither the membrane resistance nor the capacitance of Gria3null2–/– OPs at –63 mV were different from Gria3null2+/+ controls.
source: Neither the membrane resistance (Rm) nor the capacitance (Cm) of Gria3null2–/– OPs at –63 mV were different from Gria3null2+/+ controls (for Rm, p=0.16, Mann-Whitney test and for Cm, p=0.13, Student's t-test; Figure 5D,E).
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: There was no significant difference in the INa density between Gria3null2–/– and Gria3null2+/+ controls.
source: There was no significant difference in the INa density between Gria3null2–/– and Gria3null2+/+ controls (p=0.72, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 5G), suggesting that altering AMPAR signalling does not regulate the expression of voltage-gated sodium channels.
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: AMPAR signalling does not much affect the membrane properties of oligodendrocyte precursors.
source: We conclude that AMPAR signalling does not much affect the membrane properties of OPs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiological data in Figure 5.

claim: The amplitude of evoked EPSCs appeared the same in Gria3null2–/– and their Gria3null2+/– controls.
source: Surprisingly, the amplitude of the evoked EPSCs appeared the same in Gria3null2–/– and their Gria3null2+/– controls (p=0.37, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 6A,B).
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The mean amplitude of individual RR-evoked EPSCs was not reduced in Gria3null2–/– compared to Gria3null2+/– controls or Gria3null2+/+ controls.
source: Consistent with the minimal stimulation-evoked EPSC data, the mean amplitude of individual RR-evoked EPSCs was not reduced in Gria3null2–/– compared to Gria3null2+/– controls or Gria3null2+/+ controls (p=0.32, one-way ANOVA; Figure 6C,D)
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The frequency of RR-evoked EPSCs was approximately 70% less in Gria3null2–/– than in Gria3null2+/+ controls.
source: However, the frequency of RR-evoked EPSCs was ~70% less in Gria3null2–/– than in Gria3null2+/+ controls, and was reduced to an intermediate frequency in Gria3null2+/– controls (p=2×10–4, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post-hoc test; Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: There was no difference in PPR of Gria3null2–/– OPs versus Gria3null2+/+ OPs.
source: There was no difference in PPR of Gria3null2–/– OPs versus Gria3null2+/+ OPs (p=0.95, Student's t-test; Figure 6F).
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The reduction in EPSC frequency is not due to a change in presynaptic glutamate release but rather because fewer active synapses are formed or maintained in Gria3null2–/– mice.
source: This suggests that the reduction in EPSC frequency is not due to a change in presynaptic glutamate release but rather because fewer active synapses are formed or maintained in Gria3null2–/– mice.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the paired-pulse ratio data.

claim: There was a approximately 22% reduction in the density of oligodendrocytes at P7 in Gria3null2–/– compared to Gria3null2+/+ controls.
source: There was a ~22% reduction in the density of OLs at P7 and a ~27% reduction at P14 in Gria3null2–/– compared to Gria3null2+/+ controls (p=0.018 at P7; p=0.001 at P14, t–tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction; Figure 7A,B).
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: There was a approximately 27% reduction in the density of oligodendrocytes at P14 in Gria3null2–/– compared to Gria3null2+/+ controls.
source: There was a ~22% reduction in the density of OLs at P7 and a ~27% reduction at P14 in Gria3null2–/– compared to Gria3null2+/+ controls (p=0.018 at P7; p=0.001 at P14, t–tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction; Figure 7A,B).
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: By P21 and P70, the difference in oligodendrocyte density between Gria3null2–/– and Gria3null2+/+ was no longer significant.
source: By P21 (p=0.14) and P70 (p=0.48, Mann-Whitney test with Holm-Bonferroni correction) this difference was no longer significant.
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: There was a approximately 26% reduction in the density of Enpp6+ newly-differentiated oligodendrocytes in Gria3null2–/– mice compared to their Gria3null2+/+ littermates at P14.
source: This revealed a ~26% reduction of Enpp6+ newly-differentiated OLs in Gria3null2–/– mice compared to their Gria3null2+/+ littermates (p=0.004, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 7C,D)
evidence: Supported by ISH data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: There were no significant differences in the density of OPs in Gria3null2–/– subcortical white matter compared to Gria3null2+/+ controls at P3, P7, P14, P21, and P70.
source: We found no significant differences in the density of OPs in Gria3null2–/– SCWM compared to Gria3null2+/+ controls (p=0.6 at P3; p=0.85 at P7; p=0.07 at P14; p>0.99 at P21 and p=0.76 at P70, t–test or Mann-Whitney test with Holm-Bonferroni correction; Figure 7E,F).
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: The fraction of Pdgfra+ OPs that incorporated EdU was not detectably different in Gria3null2–/– versus Gria3null2+/+ subcortical white matter at P3, P7, P14, and P70.
source: The fraction of Pdgfra+ OPs that incorporated EdU ('labelling index') was not detectably different in Gria3null2–/– versus Gria3null2+/+ SCWM at any age examined (p=0.69 at P3; p=0.69 at P7; p=0.7 at P14; p=0.34 at P70, Mann-Whitney tests; Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B)
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There was no difference in the fraction of Pdgfra+ OPs in the P14 subcortical white matter that immunolabelled for Ki67 between Gria3null2–/– and Gria3null2+/+ mice.
source: nor was there any difference in the fraction of Pdgfra+ OPs in the P14 SCWM that immunolabelled for Ki67, a marker of actively dividing cells (p=0.78, Student's t-test; Figure 7—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by Ki67 immunolabeling data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The OP division rate is not affected by loss of GluA2 and GluA3.
source: These data indicate that the OP division rate is not affected by loss of GluA2 and GluA3.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EdU and Ki67 data.

claim: The proportion of Olig2+ cells that labelled for cleaved Caspase-3 in Gria3null2+/+ controls at P14 was 22.7 ± 1.2%.
source: The proportion of Olig2+ cells that labelled for cleaved Caspase-3 in Gria3null2+/+ controls at P14 was 22.7 ± 1.2% (n = 8 mice).
evidence: Supported by cleaved Caspase-3 immunolabeling data.

claim: In Gria3null2–/– mice, the cleaved Caspase-3-positive fraction was increased by a factor approximately 1.19 compared to controls.
source: In Gria3null2–/– mice the cleaved Caspase-3-positive fraction was increased by a factor ~1.19 (increased by 19.4 ± 4.2%, p=0.002, Student's t-test with Welch's correction; Figure 7G,H.).
evidence: Supported by cleaved Caspase-3 immunolabeling data shown in Figure 7H.

claim: Some newly-forming Enpp6+ oligodendrocytes express one or more GluA subunits.
source: We confirmed by double ISH for Enpp6 and Gria2, Gria3 or Gria4 that some newly-forming Enpp6+ OLs express one or more GluA subunits (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by double ISH data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Signalling through AMPAR in oligodendrocyte lineage cells promotes survival of newly-differentiating oligodendrocytes.
source: Together, these data indicate that signalling through AMPAR in OL lineage cells promotes survival of newly-differentiating OLs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the increased apoptosis and reduced OL numbers.

claim: There was a approximately 20% reduction in the number of myelin cross-sections in Gria3null2–/– normalized to littermate controls at P14.
source: This revealed a ~20% reduction in the number of myelin cross-sections in Gria3null2–/– normalized to littermate controls at P14 (p=0.02, Mann-Whitney test), consistent with the ~27% reduction in the number of OLs in Gria3null2–/– mice at the same age (see previous section; Figure 7).
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: There was no change in the average length of internodes in Gria3null2–/– compared to Gria3null2+/+ at P14.
source: There was no change in the average length of internodes (p=0.47, Student's t-test) or the average number of internodes per OL (p=0.26, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 8C,D).
evidence: Supported by dye-filling data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: There was no change in the average number of internodes per oligodendrocyte in Gria3null2–/– compared to Gria3null2+/+ at P14.
source: There was no change in the average length of internodes (p=0.47, Student's t-test) or the average number of internodes per OL (p=0.26, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 8C,D).
evidence: Supported by dye-filling data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: At P70, there was no longer any significant difference in the number of myelin cross-sections per unit area observed by EM between Gria3null2–/– and Gria3null2+/+ mice.
source: At P70 there was no longer any significant difference in the number of myelin cross-sections per unit area observed by EM (p=0.57, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 8B), consistent with the fact that the numbers of OLs identified by CC1 immunolabelling were similar in Gria3null and Gria3null2–/– at this age (Figure 7B).
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Each oligodendrocyte synthesizes a similar total length of myelin sheath in Gria3null2–/– mice as in controls.
source: Our data are consistent with a model in which each OL synthesizes a similar total length of myelin sheath in Gria3null2–/– mice as in controls and the overall synthesis of myelin is reduced in proportion to the reduced number of OLs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing proportional reduction in myelin and OLs.

claim: The current density of kainate-evoked current in Gria3null2–/–4–/– was dramatically reduced to approximately 23% of that observed in Gria3null2–/– littermates.
source: Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings of YFP+ OPs in the P14 SCWM revealed that the current density of kainate-evoked current elicited by application of 100 µM kainate at –63 mV was dramatically reduced in Gria3null2–/–4–/– to ~23% of that observed in Gria3null2–/– littermates (p<10–4, Student's t-test with Welch correction; Figure 9A,B)
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Application of 50 μM GYKI blocked the kainate-evoked current in Gria3null2–/–4–/– only by approximately 39% as opposed to approximately 80% in Gria3null2–/–.
source: In support of this, application of 50 μM GYKI blocked the kainate-evoked current in Gria3null2–/–4–/– only by ~39% as opposed to ~80% in Gria3null2–/– (p=0.005, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 9C).
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: The I-V relationship of the kainate-evoked current was nearly linear in Gria3null2–/–4–/– OPs, not inwardly-rectifying as in Gria3null2–/–.
source: Moreover, the I-V relationship of the kainate-evoked current was nearly linear in Gria3null2–/–4–/– OPs, not inwardly-rectifying as in Gria3null2–/– (different rectification indices, p=0.005, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 9D,E).
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 9D,E.

claim: Almost no EPSCs were detected following application of 100 μM RR to brain slices from Gria3null2–/–4–/– mice.
source: Consistent with the apparent lack of AMPAR in Gria3null2–/–4–/– OPs, and with AMPARs rather than KARs being the main receptor type activated at axon-OP synapses, almost no EPSCs were detected following application of 100 μM RR to brain slices (significantly less than in Gria3null2–/–; p=0.03, Mann-Whitney test) (Figure 9F,G).
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 9G.

claim: AMPAR signalling is essentially abolished in Gria3null2–/–4–/– oligodendrocyte precursors.
source: These data show that AMPAR signalling is essentially abolished in Gria3null2–/–4–/– OPs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiological data in Figure 9.

claim: At P14, there was a approximately 22% reduction in the density of oligodendrocytes in Gria3null2–/–4–/– mice relative to Gria3null controls.
source: At P14 there was a ~22% reduction in the density of OLs relative to Gria3null controls and at p53 a ~26% reduction (p=0.026 at P14; p=0.029 at P53, Mann-Whitney test, Figure 10A,B)
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: At P53, there was a approximately 26% reduction in the density of oligodendrocytes in Gria3null2–/–4–/– mice relative to Gria3null controls.
source: At P14 there was a ~22% reduction in the density of OLs relative to Gria3null controls and at p53 a ~26% reduction (p=0.026 at P14; p=0.029 at P53, Mann-Whitney test, Figure 10A,B)
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: There was no concomitant change in the density of OPs in Gria3null2–/–4–/– mice at P14 and P53.
source: without a concomitant change in the density of OPs (p=0.11 at P14; p=0.7 at P53, Mann-Whitney test) (Figure 10C,D).
evidence: Supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 10D.

claim: The fraction of Olig2+ cells that expressed cleaved Caspase-3 in subcortical white matter of P14 Gria3null controls was 24.8 ± 0.8%.
source: The fraction of Olig2+ cells that expressed cleaved Caspase-3 in SCWM of P14 Gria3null controls was 24.8 ± 0.8% (n = 5 mice) and this increased in Gria3null2–/–4–/– mice by a factor of ~1.24 (increased by 24.2 ± 4.8%, p=0.004, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 10E,F).
evidence: Supported by cleaved Caspase-3 immunolabeling data.

claim: In Gria3null2–/–4–/– mice, the cleaved Caspase-3-positive fraction increased by a factor of approximately 1.24 compared to controls.
source: The fraction of Olig2+ cells that expressed cleaved Caspase-3 in SCWM of P14 Gria3null controls was 24.8 ± 0.8% (n = 5 mice) and this increased in Gria3null2–/–4–/– mice by a factor of ~1.24 (increased by 24.2 ± 4.8%, p=0.004, Mann-Whitney test; Figure 10E,F).
evidence: Supported by cleaved Caspase-3 immunolabeling data shown in Figure 10F.

claim: There was no change in the length of the internodes or the number of internodes per oligodendrocyte in Gria3null2–/–4–/– compared to Gria3null mice.
source: As observed for Gria3null2–/– mice, there was no significant change in the average length (p=0.93, Student's t-test) or number (p=0.41, Student's t-test) of internodes per individual Gria3null2–/–4–/– OL, analyzed by dye-filling OLs in brain slices (Figure 10G,H).
evidence: Supported by dye-filling data shown in Figure 10H.

claim: Signalling through AMPAR stimulates oligodendrocyte production and myelination in the white matter by enhancing survival of newly-formed oligodendrocytes, without a detectable effect on oligodendrocyte morphology.
source: Taken together, our data demonstrate that signalling through AMPAR stimulates OL production and myelination in the white matter by enhancing survival of newly-formed OLs, without a detectable effect on OL morphology.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all the experimental data.

claim: The reduction in oligodendrocyte number observed in the Gria2/3 and Gria2/3/4 mutants results from an aspect of AMPAR signalling other than Ca2+ permeability.
source: The fact that knockout of Gria2 alone did not affect OL development implies that the reduction in OL number observed in the Gria2/3 and Gria2/3/4 mutants results from an aspect of AMPAR signalling other than Ca2+ permeability, for example the induced depolarization or the Na+ influx that it produces.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the phenotypes of different knockout combinations.

claim: AMPAR signalling in oligodendrocyte precursors and/or early-differentiating oligodendrocytes is a positive regulator of oligodendrocyte development.
source: Thus, AMPAR signalling in OPs and/or early-differentiating OLs is a positive regulator of OL development; we speculate that this favours myelination of active axons that are releasing glutamate, thus accelerating development of a functioning CNS.
evidence: This is a conclusion with a speculative component about the functional significance.

claim: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells in the subcortical white matter express mRNA encoding AMPAR subunits GluA2, GluA3 and GluA4 but not GluA1.
source: We have shown that OL lineage cells in the SCWM express mRNA encoding AMPAR subunits GluA2, GluA3 and GluA4 but not GluA1 - the same spectrum of AMPAR subunits reported for rat and mouse OPs in culture (Patneau et al., 1994; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by ISH data and citations to prior work.

claim: Knocking out GluA2 and GluA3 in oligodendrocyte precursors reduced the AMPAR-mediated current to approximately 53% of normal.
source: Knocking out GluA2 and GluA3 in OPs reduced the AMPAR-mediated current to ~53% of normal, while knocking out all three subunits GluA2/3/4 reduced it to ~13% of normal.
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data in Figures 5 and 9.

claim: Knocking out all three subunits GluA2/3/4 in oligodendrocyte precursors reduced the AMPAR-mediated current to approximately 13% of normal.
source: Knocking out GluA2 and GluA3 in OPs reduced the AMPAR-mediated current to ~53% of normal, while knocking out all three subunits GluA2/3/4 reduced it to ~13% of normal.
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data in Figures 5 and 9.

claim: In oligodendrocyte precursors lacking GluA2 and GluA3, the amplitude of RR-induced synaptic events was unchanged while their frequency was reduced to less than 30% of normal.
source: Surprisingly, we found that in OPs lacking GluA2 and GluA3 the amplitude of RR-induced synaptic events was unchanged while their frequency was reduced to <30% of normal, while in OPs lacking all AMPAR subunits their frequency was reduced to only ~1% of control.
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 6.

claim: In oligodendrocyte precursors lacking all AMPAR subunits, the frequency of RR-induced synaptic events was reduced to only approximately 1% of control.
source: Surprisingly, we found that in OPs lacking GluA2 and GluA3 the amplitude of RR-induced synaptic events was unchanged while their frequency was reduced to <30% of normal, while in OPs lacking all AMPAR subunits their frequency was reduced to only ~1% of control.
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 9.

claim: There are fewer AMPAR-containing synapses in double-knockout oligodendrocyte precursors and almost none in triple-knockouts.
source: The simplest interpretation is that there are fewer AMPAR-containing synapses in double-KO OPs (and almost none in triple-KOs), but that those synapses that survive contain a normal number of AMPARs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the synaptic event frequency and amplitude data.

claim: Almost all glutamatergic synaptic input to oligodendrocyte precursors is via AMPARs composed of GluA2, GluA3 and GluA4 subunits.
source: In any case our data provide striking genetic confirmation that almost all glutamatergic synaptic input to OPs is via AMPARs composed of GluA2, GluA3 and GluA4 subunits.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic knockout data.

claim: Oligodendrocyte precursor proliferation and OP number were normal in Gria3null2–/– and Gria3null2–/–4–/– mice.
source: We found that OP proliferation and OP number were normal in Gria3null2–/– and Gria3null2–/–4–/– mice.
evidence: Supported by cell counting and EdU incorporation data in Figures 7 and 10.

claim: The reduced number of differentiated oligodendrocytes in the double- and triple-knockouts was a result of increased death of oligodendrocyte lineage cells.
source: We found that the reduced number of differentiated OLs in the double- and triple-KOs was a result of increased death of OL lineage cells – most likely newly-formed, pre-myelinating OLs.
evidence: Supported by cleaved Caspase-3 data in Figures 7 and 10.

claim: Synaptic input and activation of AMPARs promotes neuronal survival during early postnatal development.
source: Synaptic input – and activation of AMPARs in particular – has been shown to promote neuronal survival during early postnatal development (Heck et al., 2008)
evidence: Supported by citation to Heck et al., 2008.

claim: Sensory input from the whiskers to somatosensory barrel cortex promotes the survival of newly-differentiating oligodendrocytes.
source: and a recent study showed that sensory input from the whiskers to somatosensory barrel cortex promotes the survival of newly-differentiating OLs (Hill et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hill et al., 2014.

claim: AMPAR signalling in oligodendrocyte lineage cells could be one of the mechanisms ensuring that only pre-myelinating oligodendrocytes that make contact with active axons survive to myelinate in the longer term.
source: Thus, AMPAR signalling in OL lineage cells could be one of the mechanisms ensuring that only pre-myelinating OLs that make contact with active axons survive to myelinate in the longer term (Barres et al., 1992, 1993; Trapp et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a speculative inference supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The amount of myelin in the subcortical white matter of Gria3null2–/– mice was reduced in proportion to the reduced number of oligodendrocytes.
source: In our present study we found that the amount of myelin in the SCWM of Gria3null2–/– mice was reduced in proportion to the reduced number of OLs.
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 8.

claim: The g-ratio, as well as the internode number and length, were unchanged in Gria3null2–/– mice.
source: The g-ratio, as well as the internode number and length, were unchanged, suggesting that once a pre-myelinating OL makes a commitment to myelinate an axon, the process continues until a normal internode number and length, and a normal number of myelin wraps are achieved.
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy and dye-filling data in Figure 8.

claim: AMPAR signalling stimulates myelin formation in mice by increasing the number of myelinating oligodendrocytes that develop from OPs, not by regulating myelin synthesis per se.
source: In short, we have shown that AMPAR signalling stimulates myelin formation in mice by increasing the number of myelinating OLs that develop from OPs, not by regulating myelin synthesis per se.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: AMPAR signalling in oligodendrocyte lineage cells promotes oligodendrocyte development and myelination during postnatal development.
source: In summary, our study demonstrates that AMPAR signalling in OL lineage cells promotes OL development and myelination during postnatal development.
evidence: This is the summary conclusion of the study.

claim: Approximately 80% of oligodendrocyte precursors in the postnatal subcortical white matter of wild type mice originate after birth from neural stem cells in the cortical ventricular zone.
source: Most OPs (~80%) in the postnatal SCWM of wild type mice originate after birth (E21/P0) from neural stem cells in the cortical ventricular zone (VZ), with the remaining ~20% of OPs migrating into the developing cortex from the ventral forebrain starting around embryonic day 16 (E16) (Kessaris et al., 2006; Tripathi et al., 2011; reviewed by Bergles and Richardson, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Approximately 20% of oligodendrocyte precursors in the postnatal subcortical white matter migrate into the developing cortex from the ventral forebrain starting around embryonic day 16.
source: Most OPs (~80%) in the postnatal SCWM of wild type mice originate after birth (E21/P0) from neural stem cells in the cortical ventricular zone (VZ), with the remaining ~20% of OPs migrating into the developing cortex from the ventral forebrain starting around embryonic day 16 (E16) (Kessaris et al., 2006; Tripathi et al., 2011; reviewed by Bergles and Richardson, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: AMPAR tetramers lacking GluA2 display inwardly-rectifying current responses to kainate and AMPA due to a voltage-dependent block of the channel by polyamines at positive potentials.
source: AMPAR tetramers lacking GluA2 display inwardly-rectifying current responses to kainate and AMPA, due to a voltage-dependent block of the channel by polyamines at positive potentials (Donevan and Rogawski, 1995).
evidence: Supported by citation to Donevan and Rogawski, 1995.

claim: When GluA2 is present in the edited 'R' form, the current-voltage relationship is linear, that is, non-rectifying.
source: When GluA2 is present (in the edited 'R' form), the current-voltage (I-V) relationship is linear, that is, non-rectifying.
evidence: This is established knowledge about AMPAR biophysics.
